title: fix(ui): preserve New Session during model setup redirects
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a saved `/settings/model-setup` or `/model-setup` link from New Session briefly retires and rebuilds the unchanged page before opening Models. This repeats the redirect/remount failure fixed for General in #194624.

## User Impact

Model-account setup opens faster without the intermediate New Session rebuild. Explicit first-run setup (`firstRun=1` / `firstRun=explicit`), consent, the account picker, and navigation history retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonicalize the legacy settings destination before route matching, using the same policy in the loader. The outlet can retain its current page while the actual destination loads. No cache, scheduling state, component lifetime override, or new eager dependency is introduced.

The accompanying harness measures all ordered route pairs, legacy aliases and moved-section links, plus Agent tabs, history/bookmarks, reconnect, split/detail panes and drawers. Its external DOM probe distinguishes retained identity, moves, identical-content replacements and transient subtrees. Physical attachment evidence is explicitly distinct from Solid owner disposal; detailed evidence is bounded and marked when truncated. CPU is collected in a separate probe-disabled pass.

## Evidence

Twenty rotated base/head/A-A pairs per engine, synthetic production bundles, headless desktop. Times are browser-local application readiness; WebKit results do not claim CPU.

| Engine | Median before → after | Change | p95 before → after | A/A median change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chromium | 174.9 → 113.2 ms | −35.3% | 188.6 → 132.4 ms | −2.7% |
| WebKit | 299 → 225 ms | −24.7% | 327 → 256 ms | 0.0% |
| Firefox | 224 → 144.5 ms | −35.5% | 248 → 155 ms | +0.9% |

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New Session/composer extra remount | 1 → 0; same destination/account picker |
| Sidebar extra remount | 1 → 0 |
| Chromium renderer task CPU | 180.7 → 112.6 ms median; script 85.5 → 43.2 ms |
| Fresh Chromium profile | Redundant New Session work disappears, including `listSelectableAgents`; task 201.0 → 125.4 ms in this profiled pair |
| Router/outlet regression | Fails on base because identical markup has a different node; passes with fix |
| Focused tests | 9 existing app-route tests, 6 model-setup route tests, 1 real-router mount regression, 3 probe contracts pass |
| Types/lint | UI and scripts typechecks; focused type-aware lint and formatting pass |
| Production build / Knip | Pass |
| Initial startup | 90,890 → 90,890 B gzip; 1 CSS request on both |
| Route boot tradeoff | Chat and New Session each +220 B gzip, no extra requests; no ceiling raised |
| Existing size warnings | Identical document/CSS warnings on base and head; no CSS growth |

The completed census covers all 4,648 ordered route transitions (56 sources, each with 83 non-self targets; 84 requested destination URLs in the union), each with a separate probe-disabled CPU record, plus 69 desktop interaction/history/reconnect cases and two mobile drawer cases. All passed. Detailed nested records are truncated in 540 transitions; those rebuild counts are lower bounds, while aggregate attachment counters remain complete. Browser history and direct bookmark reloads also pass on the fixed bundle.

First-run sibling timing remains within 3.3% across engines. About was measured for 20 pairs, plus ten confirmation pairs in WebKit and Firefox: paired median changes are +1.4% and +4.7%, respectively, with larger A/A spread. Its tail timing is noisy; no claim of an improved About p95. Chromium About task CPU changes by about 1%.

The census also isolated Devices warning identity churn (separate focused fix), model-loading skeleton replacements and Usage async-summary replacements. The latter two structural experiments did not demonstrate a ≥5% timing gain in ten rotated triplets and are not included. Settings redirect findings are reported to the Settings navigation owner. The full transition table is retained as local lane evidence, not committed production diagnostics.

Production UI LOC: 541 → 548 (+7). Tests: 0 → 174. Harness/docs/config: 4,225 → 5,180 (+955), for the requested reusable all-route census. The smallest production fix is seven net lines; the larger harness is isolated from runtime bundles. Solid effect, cleanup, listener, query, owner API and manual-loader counts in the two touched production modules remain zero.

Independent P0–P2 review corrected an insert-before-remove blind spot in the probe; the regression now covers both replacement orders. CI caught an unauthorized lint-suppression comment in the probe; it was removed, and explicit receiver forwarding now passes type-aware lint and all 17 probe/suppression checks.

Before and after show the same final Models/account-picker state with synthetic data and reduced motion; only the unnecessary intermediate lifetime changes.

![Before: Models account picker after the redundant New Session remount](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e01dec9d-e2e3-45ab-a8c9-a33b0f84d2ef)

![After: same Models account picker without the redundant remount](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8dcd5461-4cf0-4df7-8fa1-7dc440fc3b28)

CI run `42384487198` found one probe lint-suppression regression, fixed in `8e6d867408f`. Updated-head run `42386178813` passes that job and every other non-aggregate job except `checks-ui (2/3)`: its two corner-shape cases (supported=false/true) have exactly the same test names and assertion messages as the latest completed scheduled main run `42381572249` (`551f7825772852ac76f9753381fdbe37279ae743`). The newer scheduled main run was still in progress at attribution. The actual CI checkout was merge `3e8589c315727a700781646ac5e608b7b9a010df` on baseline `d58287d7e9b`; the failing fixture/style inputs are unchanged in that merge. Native inherited-failure recovery retains the failed CI result and this evidence; no failing check is claimed green.

A single run of `src/styles/corner-shape.browser.test.ts` on pristine branch base `b4411857f195` independently reproduces both failures (2 failed, root-token case passed). The separate main fix `f8b1a6ba3d8` updates the stale composer-alert fixture; this PR does not touch its styles or fixture.
